item.title: Ongoing Issue: Overflowing Litter Bin Frequently Missed – Increased Collection Required, 25th August
item.description:
Dear Bromley Council, I am writing to raise a formal complaint regarding the ongoing failure to adequately service the public litter bin located in the alleyway adjacent to 79 King Hall Road. This issue has been reported on numerous occasions by local residents, yet the problem continues to recur. The bin is frequently missed during scheduled collections and regularly becomes full to capacity, resulting in waste overflowing onto the surrounding area. Litter is often dispersed throughout the alleyway, creating an unsightly environment and a potential public health concern. The current servicing arrangements appear to be insufficient for the volume of waste generated at this location. As a result, residents are forced to repeatedly report the same issue, often on a weekly basis, without seeing any lasting improvement. In view of the persistent nature of this problem, I respectfully request that the collection schedule for this bin be reviewed and that consideration be given to increasing the frequency of inspections and collections to a minimum of four times per week, including weekends. This would help prevent repeated overflows and maintain a cleaner and safer environment for residents and pedestrians. Should this matter continue to remain unresolved, I will have no alternative but to escalate my concerns through the Council's formal complaints procedure and, if necessary, refer the matter to the appropriate environmental and local government oversight bodies for further review. I would be grateful if you could confirm what action will be taken to address this issue and prevent it from recurring. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Otford Close, Penge, Greater London
